text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The State Duma lower house of parliament failed to approve the government's plans to slash budget spending.
- The Duma passed on second reading a list of seven mineral deposits to be developed under sharing-production agreements.
- The climate for foreign investments has improved in Russia according to the experts of the Central Bank of Russia.
- Gazprom is planning to issue bonds worth $3 billion to raise more money.
- Moscow's biggest car producer AZLK is to resume purchases of home-made engines for its cars.
- Shareholders of Tumen oil company, 40 percent of whose shares will be auctioned in July, have approved a new board of directors.
- The West seems to have turned its face towards Russia, says the paper about the summit of the leading industrial powers in Denver.
- Russia's Justice Minister Valentin Kovalev has applied to the Prosecutor General to probe the origin of a video tape alleged to show him in a night-club sauna with naked young women.
SEVODNYA
- The Central Bank of Russia will increase Russia's reserves which are now worth $20 billion, including $2.5 billion in gold.
- The government will press on with its spending cuts rejected by the Duma and says the cuts will be based on real budget revenues.
- A law on religious organisations, approved by the Duma on Monday, revives Soviet-era curbs on religion, says one of the leaders of the Democratic Russia party.
- An aide to the former St Petersburg mayor Anatoly Sobchak was sentenced to five years in prison for abusing his duties.
NESAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia's biggest telecommunication holding Svyazinvest will auction its 25 percent of shares on July 25.
- The government will launch a new project to develop and restructure the Komi republic's timber industry.
- Russia will join a European project Airbus Industries, says Economics Minister Yakov Urinson.

- The Kremlin will have to work hard to pay for its new admission to the Group of Seven industrial powers and the Paris Club of creditor nations, says the paper, commenting on the outcome of the Denver summit.
- The discrediting of Justice Minister Valentin Kovalyov is the result of the mafia's efforts to protect one its men, according to an Interior Ministry source.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The paper suggests that the Interior Ministry arranged the release of the video tape in the Kovalyov affair.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
